bibl.title: Data-driven discovery of partial differential equations

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the governing partial differential equations of a spatiotemporal system, recovered from time series measurements
span.quote: We propose a sparse regression method capable of discovering the governing partial differential equation(s) of a given system by time series measurements in the spatial domain. The regression framework relies on sparsity-promoting techniques to select the nonlinear and partial derivative terms of the governing equations that most accurately represent the data, bypassing a combinatorially large search through all possible candidate models.

span.label: whether the governing equations of a system can be discovered from data where first-principles derivation is intractable
span.quote: Less well understood is how to uncover underlying physical laws and/or governing equations from time series data that exhibit spatiotemporal activity.

span.label: a sparse regression method that selects the terms of a PDE from a large candidate library, with parsimony enforced by Pareto analysis and the library's sufficiency written down as an assumption
span.quote: If we assume that **Θ** is an overcomplete library, meaning **Θ** has a sufficiently rich column space that the dynamics will be in its range, then the PDE should be well represented by Eq. 2 with a sparse vector of coefficients ξ. This is equivalent to picking enough candidate functions that the full PDE

span.quote: We demonstrate the success of the method by rediscovering a broad range of physical laws solely from time series data.

span.label: sparsity-promoting regression selects the few library terms that represent the data, which is what BYPASSES a combinatorially large search over all candidate models
span.quote: We propose a sparse regression method capable of discovering the governing partial differential equation(s) of a given system by time series measurements in the spatial domain. The regression framework relies on sparsity-promoting techniques to select the nonlinear and partial derivative terms of the governing equations that most accurately represent the data, bypassing a combinatorially large search through all possible candidate models.

span.label: parsimony is enforced by Pareto analysis - accuracy against complexity - which is the same device the evolutionary and sparse symbolic-regression methods use to avoid overfitting
span.quote: Both the evolutionary ( _14_) and sparse ( _16_) symbolic regression methods avoid overfitting by selecting parsimonious models that balance model accuracy with complexity via Pareto analysis.

span.label: THE METHOD CAN ONLY DISCOVER WHAT IS ALREADY IN ITS LIBRARY, and the paper states the sufficiency of the library as an ASSUMPTION: `if we assume that Theta is an overcomplete library, meaning Theta has a sufficiently rich column space that the dynamics will be in its range`
span.quote: If we assume that **Θ** is an overcomplete library, meaning **Θ** has a sufficiently rich column space that the dynamics will be in its range, then the PDE should be well represented by Eq. 2 with a sparse vector of coefficients ξ. This is equivalent to picking enough candidate functions that the full PDE

span.label: THE NAMED FAILURE IS RIGHT TERMS AND WRONG NUMBERS: on Kuramoto-Sivashinsky the correct terms are identified and there is substantial coefficient error under noise, which the paper calls a limitation of the method rather than of the example
span.quote: The Kuramoto-Sivashinsky equation is particularly challenging to identify with low error on the coefficients and illustrates a limitation of the method. Although the correct terms are identified, there is substantial coefficient error in the case with noise.

span.label: the validation is REDISCOVERY - a method for finding equations nobody knows, tested on Navier-Stokes, the quantum harmonic oscillator and the diffusion equation
span.quote: The method is computationally efficient, robust, and demonstrated to work on a variety of canonical problems spanning a number of scientific domains including Navier-Stokes, the quantum harmonic oscillator, and the diffusion equation.

span.label: the method is run on systems whose governing equations are already known - Navier-Stokes, the quantum harmonic oscillator, the diffusion equation - and asked to REDISCOVER them
span.note: eliminates: a discovery procedure that produces a plausible equation for any data, since on these systems the right answer is known in advance and the method must return it · outcome: held
span.quote: The method is computationally efficient, robust, and demonstrated to work on a variety of canonical problems spanning a number of scientific domains including Navier-Stokes, the quantum harmonic oscillator, and the diffusion equation.

span.label: Gaussian noise is added to every example and the method is re-run, and the data is also subsampled spatially
span.note: eliminates: a recovery that depends on clean, densely sampled data - noise is stated to significantly complicate both differentiation and library building · outcome: partial
span.quote: Each example is also identified after the addition of Gaussian noise to the data set, which significantly complicates accurate differentiation and library building. Remarkably, the method is able to discover each physical system even if significantly subsampled spatially.

span.label: multiple time series taken with DIFFERENT INITIAL DATA are used where terms are potentially nonunique
span.note: eliminates: two different equations that fit one trajectory equally well being indistinguishable - a linear wave equation against Korteweg-de Vries · outcome: held
span.quote: Moreover, the method is capable of disambiguating between potentially nonunique dynamical terms by using multiple time series taken with different initial data. Thus, for a traveling wave, the method can distinguish between a linear wave equation and the Korteweg–de Vries equation, for instance.
